important_interpretation: Scores describe orchestration architecture, not investment quality or financial authority.
The post-472 baseline credits contracts already implemented in the unmerged PR stack so Temporal is not credited for solving those domain gaps.

The with-Temporal case assumes selected workflows, Temporal Cloud, client-side payload encryption, immutable exact-release Workers, and Worker Versioning. It is not a score for broad migration or self-hosting.

Temporal Activities are at-least-once. A high idempotency score assumes Trade AI reservation journals, stable business keys, and unique database constraints; Temporal alone does not provide exactly-once side effects.

post_472_with_temporal.label: Post-#472 domain architecture plus Temporal for selected long-running advisory workflows
assumptions: Temporal Cloud is used for the production Temporal Service.
Canonical portfolio, research, thesis, feedback, outcome, and notification truth remains in Trade AI PostgreSQL/domain stores.
Payloads carry IDs and bounded metadata rather than raw research blobs or full RAG context.
A Payload Codec encrypts sensitive workflow payloads before they leave Trade AI Workers.
Workers run from immutable exact-main releases and use Worker Deployment Versions.
Broker, orders, stops, risk enforcement, 2FA, price truth, position truth, and low-latency execution remain outside Temporal.

dimensions.rationale: Temporal persists Workflow progress and coordinates replay after Worker or infrastructure failure; post-#472 improves domain durability but still depends on scheduler/job handoffs.
The PR stack adds stable IDs and dedupe. Temporal improves structured retry boundaries but its Activities are at-least-once, so external-call journals and database uniqueness remain mandatory.
Workflow Event History provides a durable stage-by-stage orchestration record while canonical domain records retain investment provenance.
Per-Activity policies, timeouts, non-retryable business failures, and visible attempt state replace multiplicative cron, provider, and queue retries when designed as one retry layer.
This is Temporal's strongest fit for multi-stage research-to-CIO and NEED_DATA workflows that currently require explicit repair or restart logic.
Durable timers materially fit 1d, 5d, 20d, and quarterly outcome maturation and long feedback waits.
Signals and Updates can durably advance a known Workflow, but the CIO event meaning must remain singular and cycle-free.
Explicit Workflows and Activities make orchestration state reviewable without relocating business truth into Temporal.
Worker Versioning is the official recommended default for new production Workflow deployments and pins Workflows to Worker Deployment Versions.
Versioned immutable Workers reduce in-flight code ambiguity, but Temporal cannot fix dirty-tree or incorrect Worker launch paths by itself.
Visibility, bounded Search Attributes, Event History, and metrics add orchestration diagnostics; domain maturity metrics still come from Trade AI stores.
A Command Center diagnostic link to a Workflow Execution can show last stage, retries, and source SHA without making Temporal UI the investment interface.
Post-#472 already has authoritative accounting. Temporal preserves the score only if cost-cap and policy failures are non-retryable and provider calls use pre-call reservations.
Temporal adds a control plane and metadata exposure. Cloud with client-side encryption and least privilege is defensible, but increases the security surface relative to no Temporal.
Remote orchestration adds scheduling and network latency; this is acceptable only for advisory/research workflows, never low-latency execution or hard protection.
Cloud avoids a local Temporal Service but adds always-on Workers, action/storage usage, and network overhead.
Deterministic Workflow constraints, Activity boundaries, SDK testing, versioning, and idempotency design add a meaningful learning and code burden.

Cloud removes server operations but not Worker releases, stuck Workflow response, codec/key management, or incident handling. Selected adoption narrowly improves net operations; self-hosting would score materially lower.
Adding Temporal requires shadow dual-run, single-writer transitions, stable workflow IDs, and rollback; broad adoption would be riskier.
SDK and Workflow semantics introduce Temporal dependency even though the open-source server and Cloud use portable APIs.
Temporal Cloud owns persistence and server upgrades, but Trade AI still owns Workers, encryption codec/key lifecycle, connectivity, and release compatibility.
Temporal adds an external orchestration dependency. Canonical state and all financial protection must continue operating independently.

recommendation.current_go_no_go_reason: No successful isolated Temporal runtime POC, failure-injection evidence, Cloud security configuration, or authorized production migration exists yet.
scope: PortfolioCIOReviewWorkflow only after the first three prove value
keep_out: simple stateless cron and database maintenance
recommendation.why: The architecture score shows enough potential durability, timer, causality, crash-continuation, and Worker-version benefit to justify an isolated POC for selected long-running workflows. It does not justify adoption yet: no Temporal runtime or failure-injection result exists, and the separate production-option score narrowly favors no Temporal over Cloud once privacy, cost, and offline behavior are included. If every POC and migration gate passes, selected-workflow adoption with Temporal Cloud is the conditional target; broad adoption and self-hosting are not.
